settings.dramaVramHint: Auto sets itself up: the whole model when it fits the free VRAM, otherwise its experts (18 GB) live in RAM and the card keeps a cache of the ones in use. A number sets the amount by hand; 24 GB keeps the whole model on the card. The sound is the same; less VRAM is slower (measured on an RTX 4090): 24 GB about 8× faster than real time, 12 GB 4.7×, 8 GB 3×, 6 GB 2.2×.

help.title: About Speech Studio
help.intro: Speech Studio voices text and recognises speech on your computer: the models run on your graphics card, and the cloud is used only where you turn it on.
how: Download the models on the first run: the studio picks the set for your graphics card.
Speech: write or paste a text, pick a voice and voice it.
Listening: open a recording, a link or the microphone and get the text with the speakers.
Save the result where you want it.
features: Voice cloning from a few seconds of a recording
Your own library of voices with photos and tags
Higgs Audio v3 locally, Drama 3 on cards from 6 GB
Speakers told apart in a recording
Cloud voices and recognition through OpenRouter and Google
An agent (MCP) drives the studio while you watch
sections: Listening: recognising speech and checking a voicing
Settings (⚙): models, cloud, network, agent, statistics
help.donateIntro: I build open-source software and do AI research. Most of what I create is free and available to everyone. Your donations help me keep creating and researching without worrying about where the next meal comes from =) Thank you 🙏

tags.legend: Emotion, style, speed, pitch and expressiveness go to the start of the sentence; pause and sound go at the cursor. Right after a sound, with no space, write its onomatopoeia ("Ha-ha,", "Ahem,"): Higgs needs it. Tags the engine does not know are cut and named.
tags.universal: Pause and tempo work with any engine: tempo lasts to the next tempo tag or the end of the block.
tags.none: {{engine}} has no expression tags: pauses and tempo work.
tags.dramaRussian: Drama 3 tags and directions work poorly in Russian (checked by ear).
tags.legendDrama: An event goes at its place in the text; for a span, select the words and click. Drama reads the block’s direction as the delivery of the whole line.
tags.legendPlain: A tag goes at the cursor; tags the engine does not know are cut and named.
tags.qwen: Qwen3-TTS has no tags: write laughter and sounds as onomatopoeia in the text ("ha-ha", "hmm") and the model voices them by context; set the delivery in the direction (works with the model’s own voices, not with a clone).

listen.filterHint: Lines like “Thanks for watching” or “Subtitles by…” are hidden when nobody speaks at their time; you can return any of them.
listen.promptPlaceholder: For example: a podcast about neural networks, Qwen, GitHub
listen.promptHint: Whisper takes the topic and how terms are spelled; the spellings from the corrections below are added on their own. Other recognisers take no hints.
listen.denoiseHint: DPDFNet: street noise, hum, hiss. Strength is how far below the original the noise may go; 18 dB keeps speech natural.
listen.vadHint: Silero VAD finds the speech, and Parakeet gets the recording in pieces of up to 90 seconds cut at pauses, not mid-word. Silence between pieces is not recognised. Whisper cuts the recording itself.
listen.fixesHint: How the recogniser mishears a word → how it is written. Applied to every recognition of this recording.
listen.settingsApply: Changes apply to the next recognition.
listen.format_srt: SRT: subtitles for players and editors.
listen.format_vtt: WebVTT: subtitles for the web; speakers as voice tags.
listen.format_ass: ASS: subtitles with styles; the speaker in the Name field.
listen.format_txt: Plain text, with or without speakers and times.
listen.format_json: JSON with lines, speakers and word timings.
listen.checkHint: Paste the text the recording should say: the check shows missed, extra and replaced words and the word error rate.
listen.alignHint: The recording's lines take the reference text, each word at the time it was heard. Speakers stay; it undoes like any edit.
listen.checkSummary: Errors {{wer}}% of {{words}} words: missed {{missed}}, extra {{extra}}, replaced {{replaced}}
listen.removeMessage: “{{name}}” goes to the recycle bin with its recording, transcript and exports.
listen.engineHint_fal: A fal.ai recognition model (Whisper, ElevenLabs Scribe…): paid, needs the key; word times are approximate.

chat.title: Assistant
chat.intro: The assistant works the studio with the same tools an MCP agent has: it opens projects, edits text, voices and recognises. Each step shows here, and changes go into the activity log. It runs paid cloud voicing only with your consent.
chat.introAgent: The connected agent (MCP) answers: your message goes to it, it does the work with its tools and answers here. Nothing is paid.

suggestions.what: What is open and what can I do here?
suggestions.voice: Voice the changed blocks of this project
suggestions.check: Check that every block is voiced without errors
suggestions.listen: How do I recognise a two-speaker recording and turn it into a script?

chat.placeholder: Write to the assistant… (Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a new line)
chat.footnote: The conversation is paid with the OpenRouter key and counts toward the agents' daily limit.
chat.footnoteAgent: The connected agent answers; the conversation is free.
chat.needsKey: The assistant needs an OpenRouter model (your key) or a connected MCP agent.
chat.who: Who answers in the Assistant panel
chat.whoModelHint: Paid with your key; the model is chosen in the panel itself.
chat.whoAgentHint: The message goes to the agent (assistant_requests_wait), which answers on its own; free.

api.intro: Other programs on this computer voice and recognise through the studio with the OpenAI protocol: give them the address below as the base URL. voice is a voice name of the library, model the engine (tts-1 → Higgs, drama3 → Drama 3, whisper-1 → Parakeet), instructions the block's direction. Only this computer can reach it.
api.keyNone: none: the API is open to the programs of this computer
api.keyOnce: The new key: copy it now, it is not shown again
api.keyHint: With a key, a program sends it in the Authorization header (Bearer); without one, any program of this computer is answered.
api.logEmpty: No requests since the studio started.

diag.title: System diagnostics
diag.hint: What the studio sees: the graphics card, driver and CUDA, ffmpeg, which components are in place, which libraries the engines lack, and the latest log lines. Keys never get in.

consent.title: Send to {{provider}}?
consent.what_speech: The blocks' text and directions go to {{provider}} to be voiced, and the audio comes back from there; it is paid with your key.
consent.what_listening: The recording goes to {{provider}} to be recognised, and the text comes back from there; it is paid with your key.
consent.what_director: The podcast's topic or the chapter's text goes to {{provider}}, whose model writes the script or casts the characters; it is paid with your key.
consent.what_assistant: Your messages and the studio tools' answers (projects, block texts) go to the model at {{provider}}; it is paid with your key.
consent.once: The studio asks once for this stage; you can take it back in Settings, Privacy.

privacy.title: Where data goes
privacy.hint: Everything not named cloud stays on this computer. Before a stage first goes to the cloud, the studio asks.
privacy.route_speech: Higgs and Drama 3 run on this computer; OpenRouter, Google Gemini, fal.ai and Runware get the blocks' text (the engine is chosen in the project).
privacy.route_listening: Parakeet and Whisper run on this computer; OpenRouter and fal.ai get the recording (the engine is chosen in the project).
privacy.route_director_server: Now: your model server (its address is in Models).
privacy.route_director_cloud: Now: OpenRouter, so the topic and chapter texts go to the cloud.
privacy.route_assistant_openrouter: An OpenRouter model: messages and tool answers go to the cloud.
privacy.route_assistant_agent: The connected agent (MCP) on this computer; where it sends data is its own choice.
privacy.route_local: Voice cleaning, stress marks and ё, speaker separation, voice similarity, splitting by pauses, export.

errors.whatToDo: What to do: copy the text, look at the diagnostics or report the problem.

supertonic.F1: Calm female voice with a slightly low tone; steady and composed. Customer service, guided instructions, meditation, professional narration.
supertonic.F2: Bright, cheerful female voice; lively, playful and youthful. Youth content, playful ads, social media, character voices.
supertonic.F3: Clear, professional announcer-style female voice; broadcast-ready. Commercials, documentaries, news-style narration.
supertonic.F4: Crisp, confident female voice; expressive with strong delivery. Business explainers, training videos, product announcements.
supertonic.F5: Kind, gentle female voice; soft-spoken, calm and soothing. Audiobooks, supportive messages, wellness, empathetic narration.
supertonic.M1: Lively, upbeat male voice; confident and clear. Promotional videos, upbeat explainers, general narration.
supertonic.M2: Deep, robust male voice; calm, composed and serious. Corporate content, serious announcements, documentaries.
supertonic.M3: Polished, authoritative male voice; confident and trustworthy. Business presentations, leadership messages, high-trust narration.
supertonic.M4: Soft, neutral-toned male voice; gentle, youthful and friendly. Education, friendly explainers, onboarding guides.
supertonic.M5: Warm, soft-spoken male voice; calm, a natural storyteller. Audiobooks, bedtime stories, reflective narration.
